script.base: Detroit is a road favorite by 8.5 with a 29.0 implied total, so the base script is a Detroit lead by halftime that gets closed on the ground. Jahmyr Gibbs just took 43 carries for 226 yards in weeks 6/7/9 (5.26 YPC) against David Montgomery's 28 carries for 85, and Washington allows 4.59 YPC with 29 runs of 10-plus in 9 games. Washington's implied total is only 20.5 with Jayden Daniels Out (elbow) and Terry McLaurin Out (quad), so M.Mariota (10 carries, 62 rush yards in weeks 7-9) is chasing and the checkdown/replacement receivers, not the early-down rush, get the extra plays.
script.flip1: Washington hangs within one score because Mariota's legs and the Croskey-Merritt/Rodriguez committee (34 and 16 carries in weeks 7-9) steal the clock. Detroit never flips fully to a late run script, Gibbs's carry total stays in the 54/65/25 range instead of the 136-yard spike, and both passing games stay live into the fourth quarter.
script.flip2: Detroit is up by three scores early, the -8.5 blowout flag hits, and late starter snaps get cut. Gibbs still banks the early and mid-game carries before any rest, Washington abandons J.Croskey-Merritt (L3 2.8 YPC), and garbage throws go to Z.Ertz, J.McNichols, J.Lane and D.Samuel. A pure clock-kill is the way Detroit receiver yardage stalls after the lead is built.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost. Gibbs finished under 66.5 because Washington's 4.59 YPC did not show up: Decker was limited, Montgomery took the closer carries the way he did in the games Gibbs finished at 54, 65 and 25, and Detroit's 0.54 EPA against the blitz made Goff throw instead of handing Gibbs the late script the -8.5 promised. The 136-yard game was the outlier the line was shading, not the median. McNichols finished under 6.5 because the 0-yard game was the role, not noise: Mariota spent the chase on Ertz, who already had 17 targets for 99 yards in weeks 7-9, and on Samuel, while Croskey-Merritt and C.Rodriguez kept the snaps in a game that stayed closer than 8.5. Rodriguez being out did not automatically mean the third-down back was targeted. If that counter-case is how it plays, both legs were script bets that the flip beat.
slip_story: One story only: Detroit leads as a -8.5 favorite, runs late through Gibbs, and Washington without Daniels and McLaurin throws underneath to McNichols. Those two win together in the base script and in the blowout flip. Do not add a total under, a Gibbs receiving or rush-plus-rec leg, a LaPorta or St. Brown over, or a Croskey-Merritt rush over; those need Detroit to throw or Washington to stay on schedule on the ground. Lane and Samuel stay off this slip even though McLaurin is out, because this stack is the checkdown and the lead-back run, not the outside shot into Detroit's 5.55/6.71 edge splits.
